allowed_dependency_manifest.content: For each fixed integer n greater than 1, consider the function E_n(x) = floor(n x) minus the sum over integers k with 1 <= k <= n of floor(k x) divided by k. The task is to determine the set of real x values for which E_n(x) attains its maximum over all real x, and to determine the corresponding maximal value M(n).
allowed_dependency_manifest.label: root_semantic_sketch

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.role_in_assembly: Provide the sharp global upper bound at rational endpoints and identify the unique endpoint achieving equality.

domain_restrictions: k is an integer summation index with 1 less than or equal to k and k less than or equal to n
floor is the greatest integer less than or equal to its real input

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n > 1

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n > 1 and every integer a with 0 <= a <= n - 1, the inequality E_n(a/n) <= H_n - 1 holds, and E_n(a/n) equals H_n - 1 if and only if a equals n - 1.
quantifier_order: for all integers n with n > 1
for all integers a with 0 <= a <= n - 1

variables.name: n
variables.role: outer parameter indexing the functions E_n and H_n

variables.name: a
variables.role: input index used to form the argument a/n

witness_dependencies: No existential witnesses are introduced; the equality condition is a direct constraint on the universally quantified variable a
The equality threshold H_n - 1 depends only on n, not on a, and the argument to E_n depends on both n and a through a/n

payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every integer a with 0 <= a <= n-1, one has E_n(a/n) <= H_n - 1, and equality holds if and only if a = n-1.

suspected_gaps: I could not derive a rigorous sharp estimate for the weighted floor sum at rational points.
A number of promising rewrites reduced the lemma to bounding a discrete harmonic sum, but I did not complete the needed inequality.
I was able to get only weaker bounds such as E_n(a/n) <= H_n, which are insufficient for the stated sharp bound H_n - 1.

result_payload.stuck_point: Need a sharp, rigorous bound for the transformed sum T = sum_{k=1}^n floor((k(n-a)-1)/n)/k (equivalently sum floor(ka/n)/k >= a - H_n + 1). I could not complete the final estimate that would force the maximum to occur only at a = n - 1.
